phase3_findings.description: _CatalogView does not enforce that kept is a subset of fields or that fields has no duplicates; a misspelled kept name silently reads as NULL (fails safe, unnoticed).
rule_sets docstring can be read as making the schema-lookup limit depend on a dialect resolving; line 189 selects it on rule_sets alone.
test_key_column_usage_lists_only_keys_inside_the_set calls pytest.skip after its main check when SQLLENS_TEST_MYSQL_OTHER_DATABASE is unset, reporting a skip for a passed check locally.
No connector case covers a listed table's foreign key referencing an unlisted column of another listed table; only a unit test pins that filter text.

report:
## Verdict: APPROVE with notes (four suggestions, two inconclusive checklist items)
This PR is ready to merge: no reviewer or checklist item found a defect at or above the important threshold, and every acceptance criterion is itemized.
Rule applied: rule 6 — findings below the threshold and inconclusive items remain → APPROVE with notes

## Code Review Findings

### 🟡 Suggestion / Minor (4)
<details><summary>4 items</summary>

1. `src/sqllens/safety/rule_sets.py` lines 92-140: the `_CatalogView` dataclass does not check that `kept` is a subset of `fields` or that `fields` has no duplicates. A misspelled kept name would silently read as `NULL`. The failure is safe but goes unnoticed. (raised by 1/6 agents)
2. `src/sqllens/agent/core/system_prompt/default.py` lines 62-67: the `rule_sets` docstring can be read as saying the schema-lookup limit depends on a dialect resolving. The code at line 189 chooses it on `rule_sets` alone. (raised by 1/6 agents)
3. `tests/connectors/test_rule_sets_mysql.py`: `test_key_column_usage_lists_only_keys_inside_the_set` runs its main check and then calls `pytest.skip` when `SQLLENS_TEST_MYSQL_OTHER_DATABASE` is unset, so a local run reports a skip even though a check passed. CI sets the variable. (raised by 1/6 agents)
4. `tests/connectors/test_rule_sets_mysql.py`: no connector case has a listed table whose foreign key points at an unlisted column of another listed table. A unit test pins the filter text that excludes such rows. (raised by 1/6 agents)

</details>

### ℹ️ Informational — Deferred
- VC-4: INCONCLUSIVE (important) — A LIMIT 18446744073709551615 on the derived table stops MySQL from merging it into the outer query or pushing the model's conditions into it, so a model expression never runs on a hidden catalog row [docs/internal/database-connectors/rule-sets.md]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  The claim depends on MySQL optimizer behavior (derived-table merge and condition pushdown with LIMIT). The repository only emits the SQL: src/sqllens/safety/rule_sets.py:143-146 defines _MATERIALIZE_LIMIT = "18446744073709551615" with a comment making the same claim, and tests/unit/test_safety_rule_sets.py:320-325,374,386 assert the LIMIT is appended to the derived tables. No MySQL source was provided (no dependency_sources) and no MySQL server run was possible. The known documented rule (a derived table containing LIMIT is not mergeable and conditions are not pushed into it) supports the claim, and the outer expressions in the select list, JOIN ON or ORDER BY would run over the materialized, already-filtered rows. However, I could not confirm that the optimizer treats the value 18446744073709551615 (equal to HA_POS_ERROR, the 'no limit' sentinel) as a real LIMIT clause on every supported MySQL version. Not verified: running EXPLAIN FORMAT=TREE on SELECT ... FROM (SELECT ... LIMIT 18446744073709551615) AS t JOIN ... ON <error-raising expr> against MySQL 8.0 and 8.4.

  </details>

- VC-9: INCONCLUSIVE (suggestion) — Comparing CAST(TABLE_NAME AS BINARY) against plain string literals matches byte for byte regardless of the connection collation/charset of information_schema columns (utf8mb3) versus literal charset [src/sqllens/safety/rule_sets.py]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  rule_sets.py:321-337,346-353 wrap only the catalog column side in CAST(... AS BINARY) (_binary); the literals (exp.Literal.string at 334, 351) are plain strings. In MySQL a binary string vs nonbinary string comparison is bytewise, so collation differences (utf8mb3 columns vs connection collation) are irrelevant: this part holds. The existence check in safety/relations.py:173-174 uses the same BINARY x = BINARY y pattern. However the claim says 'regardless of ... charset': the literal's bytes are in the connection charset, and the repo never sets it (grep for charset/character_set in src found nothing; it comes from the driver/URL). For non-ASCII identifiers under a non-utf8 connection charset (e.g. latin1) the literal bytes would differ from the utf8mb3 column bytes, so the charset-independence part cannot be settled by reading; it needs a MySQL run (not performed). Collation independence is established, charset independence is not.

  </details>

  - VC-7: _is_catalog_derived reads the From node via body.args.get('from_'), matching the arg key sqlglot (>=30.22) uses for Select's FROM [src/sqllens/safety/rule_sets.py]
  - VC-8: KEY_COLUMN_USAGE filter keeps a row only when its own schema/table/column is listed and the referenced schema, table and column are all NULL or all pass the same listed test, hiding rows referencing another database or unlisted tables/columns [src/sqllens/safety/rule_sets.py]
  - VC-10: When the rule set lists tables (and thus pairs) the IN lists are non-empty; an empty listing would generate IN () which must be handled or impossible by rule-set loading [src/sqllens/safety/rule_sets.py]
  - VC-11: The monkeypatched second_fails accepts (tree, tables, expected=None) matching the new _rewalk signature and apply_rule_set's call pattern [tests/unit/test_safety_rule_sets.py]
  - VC-12: CI step creates database sqllens_other granting ALL to 'sqllens'@'%', and the connector test user name/host matches that account used by SQLLENS_TEST_MYSQL_URL [.github/workflows/ci.yml]
  - VC-13: The step-level env SQLLENS_TEST_MYSQL_OTHER_DATABASE is added without dropping job-level env (SQLLENS_TEST_MYSQL_URL) needed by the pytest step [.github/workflows/ci.yml]
  - VC-14: The connector fixture setup creates rs_customers with a FOREIGN KEY to rs_salaries before rs_salaries exists, relying on FOREIGN_KEY_CHECKS=0 set earlier on the same connection in _TEARDOWN [tests/connectors/test_rule_sets_mysql.py]

  - VC-18: Other catalog views, the mysql, performance_schema and sys schemas, and SHOW statements are still refused under a rule set [changelog.d/393.added.md]
  - VC-19: Doc says a KEY_COLUMN_USAGE row must have NULL referenced schema, table and column or ones that pass the same test, matching _catalog_filter [docs/internal/database-connectors/rule-sets.md]

  - VC-26: Under the example set, a catalog read of a field outside the 25 kept fields (for example `TABLE_ROWS`, `COLUMN_DEFAULT` or `CONSTRAINT_NAME`) returns `NULL` for it, and `SELECT *` over a rewritten view returns every field of that view, each field outside the kept fields `NULL`. [src/sqllens/safety/rule_sets.py]
  - VC-27: A rewritten statement in which a reference to `INFORMATION_SCHEMA.TABLES`, `COLUMNS` or `KEY_COLUMN_USAGE` sits outside the catalog derived table the guard builds for it is refused (a planted defect in a unit test), and a read of `INFORMATION_SCHEMA.STATISTICS` or `SHOW TABLES` is still refused. [src/sqllens/safety/rule_sets.py]
  - VC-28: While a rule-set file is configured, the system prompt's MySQL schema-lookup guidance names `INFORMATION_SCHEMA.TABLES`, `COLUMNS` and `KEY_COLUMN_USAGE` and permits no `SHOW` statement, and the prompt differs from #374's rule-set prompt for the same configuration by that change only. [src/sqllens/agent/core/system_prompt/default.py]
  - VC-29: Without a rule-set file configured, catalog reads return what they return today, and the system prompt is byte-identical to today's for the same configuration. [src/sqllens/agent/core/system_prompt/default.py]

  </details>
- Reviewed against issue #379 — criteria from the workpad; scope unchanged.

acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Under the example set, `SELECT TABLE_NAME FROM INFORMATION_SCHEMA.TABLES WHERE TABLE_SCHEMA = DATABASE()` returns exactly `customers` and `orders`, and the same query written as `select table_name from information_schema.tables where table_schema = database()` returns the same rows.
- [ ] Under the example set, `INFORMATION_SCHEMA.COLUMNS` returns exactly the five listed columns, with no row for `email`, `discount` or `rep_id`.
- [ ] Under the example set, `INFORMATION_SCHEMA.KEY_COLUMN_USAGE` returns the primary-key rows for `customers.id` and `orders.id` and the foreign-key row from `orders.customer_id` to `customers.id`, and it returns no row whose table, column, referenced table or referenced column is outside the set, and no row whose schema or referenced schema is another database (a same-named `orders` table in another database the SQL Lens user can read included).
- [ ] Under the example set, `SELECT TABLE_NAME FROM INFORMATION_SCHEMA.TABLES WHERE IF(TABLE_NAME = 'salaries', EXP(1000), 0) > 0` returns no row and raises no error.
- [ ] Under the example set, a catalog read of a field outside the 25 kept fields (for example `TABLE_ROWS`, `COLUMN_DEFAULT` or `CONSTRAINT_NAME`) returns `NULL` for it, and `SELECT *` over a rewritten view returns every field of that view, each field outside the kept fields `NULL`.
- [ ] A rewritten statement in which a reference to `INFORMATION_SCHEMA.TABLES`, `COLUMNS` or `KEY_COLUMN_USAGE` sits outside the catalog derived table the guard builds for it is refused (a planted defect in a unit test), and a read of `INFORMATION_SCHEMA.STATISTICS` or `SHOW TABLES` is still refused.
- [ ] While a rule-set file is configured, the system prompt's MySQL schema-lookup guidance names `INFORMATION_SCHEMA.TABLES`, `COLUMNS` and `KEY_COLUMN_USAGE` and permits no `SHOW` statement, and the prompt differs from #374's rule-set prompt for the same configuration by that change only.
- [ ] Without a rule-set file configured, catalog reads return what they return today, and the system prompt is byte-identical to today's for the same configuration.
